# Spiral Design Report: Transatlantic Four-Seat Tourer

**Status:** Converged after **3** spiral laps.

## Summary
This report presents the conceptual design of the Transatlantic Four-Seat Tourer, sized for a non-stop 5,570 km mission from London to New York with a 45.0 min reserve. The sizing spiral converged in 3 laps, reducing maximum takeoff weight (MTOW) by -2.3% from 2,478.9 kg on lap 0 to a final MTOW of 2,421.9 kg. The converged baseline features an empty mass of 1,209.1 kg (49.9% of MTOW), a fuel mass of 990.8 kg (40.9% of MTOW), and a wing area of 30.27 m2 with a 15.17 m span. The primary wing spar is sized in al_2024_t3 at 92.8 kg across both wings (93.5 kg used in the sizing loop), achieving a 0.10 safety margin under beam theory.

_Narrative paragraphs written by Gemini (gemini-4-argon) from the computed results below; every number in them was checked against the design state._

## Mission & configuration
- **Range:** 5,570 km with 45 min reserve
- **Cruise:** 59.2 m/s at 2,500 m
- **Stall speed:** 28.3 m/s
- **Payload:** 1 crew + 1.0 passengers at 86.0 kg, 50.0 kg baggage (222.0 kg payload)
- **Wing:** high wing, aspect ratio 7.6, taper ratio 0.45, t/c 0.15, CL_max 1.6, L/D_max 11
- **Propulsion:** propeller efficiency 0.8, BSFC 6.80e-08 kg/J
- **Structure:** +3.8 g limit x 1.5 = 5.70 g ultimate, spar material `al_2024_t3`

## Convergence history
| Lap | MTOW (kg) | ΔMTOW (%) | Empty (kg) | Fuel (kg) | Spar (kg) | Wing area (m²) | Span (m) | Peak bending stress (MPa) | Tip deflection (mm) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 2,478.9 | n/a | 1,242.8 | 1,014.1 | 96.0 | 30.98 | 15.35 | 306.6 | 750.3 |
| 1 | 2,433.9 | -1.81 | 1,216.2 | 995.7 | 93.5 | 30.42 | 15.21 | 306.6 | 743.3 |
| 2 | 2,421.9 | -0.49 | 1,209.1 | 990.8 | 92.8 | 30.27 | 15.17 | 306.6 | 741.4 |

## Mass breakdown
- **MTOW:** 2,421.9 kg
- **Empty mass:** 1,209.1 kg (empty fraction 0.499)
- **Fuel mass:** 990.8 kg (fuel fraction 0.409)
- **Payload:** 222.0 kg
- **Spar mass used in sizing:** 93.5 kg (statistical estimate 103.6 kg)

| Item | Mass (kg) | Share of MTOW (%) |
|---|---|---|
| Wing spar (both wings) | 93.5 | 3.9 |
| Rest of empty mass | 1,115.7 | 46.1 |
| Fuel | 990.8 | 40.9 |
| Crew | 86.0 | 3.6 |
| Passengers | 86.0 | 3.6 |
| Baggage | 50.0 | 2.1 |

## Wing & power
- **Wing area / span:** 30.27 m² / 15.17 m (wing loading 785 Pa)
- **Root / tip chord / MAC:** 2.75 m / 1.24 m / 2.09 m
- **Cruise / installed power:** 159.7 kW / 278.7 kW

## Main wing spar (beam theory)
- **Material:** `al_2024_t3`
- **Spar mass:** 92.8 kg both wings (46.4 kg per wing)
- **Root / tip depth:** 351.0 mm / 158.0 mm
- **Root cap:** 122.9 mm wide x 16.79 mm thick; web 4.05 mm
- **Peak bending stress:** 306.6 MPa against 337.8 MPa allowable (margin +0.10)
- **Peak shear stress:** 47.5 MPa
- **Tip deflection at 5.70 g ultimate:** 741.4 mm

## FEA vs beam theory
Solver: Timoshenko beam FEA (NumPy direct stiffness)

| Quantity | FEA | Beam theory | Agreement (%) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Peak stress (MPa) | 304.2 | 306.6 | 99.2 |
| Tip deflection (mm) | 749.5 | 741.4 | 98.9 |

FEA safety margin: +0.11

## Discussion
### What drove the design
The non-stop 5,570 km range requirement and 45.0 min reserve at a cruise L/D max of 11.0 (Raymer 2ed, Ch. 3 (p. 22)) and a BSFC of 6.8e-08 kg/J drive a cruise mass fraction of 0.6557 and a total fuel mass of 990.8 kg, which far exceeds the 222.0 kg payload (1 crew at 86.0 kg, 1.0 passenger at 86.0 kg, and 50.0 kg baggage). The 28.3 m/s (under 55 kt) stall speed requirement with a maximum lift coefficient of 1.6 limits wing loading to 785.0 Pa (Raymer 2ed, Eq. 5.6 (p. 85)), requiring a 30.27 m2 wing area and a 15.17 m span at an aspect ratio of 7.6. Structural sizing of the cantilever spar is governed by the 5.7 g ultimate load factor (3.8 g limit with a 1.5 ultimate factor) and conservative loading with no inertia relief from wing structure or fuel, while web shear buckling sets the web thickness at 17 of 21 spanwise stations.

### Trade-offs
Feeding the beam-theory spar mass back into the sizing loop reduced the spar allocation from the statistical estimate of 103.6 kg (and 96.0 kg on lap 0) to 92.8 kg on lap 2, trimming MTOW to 2,421.9 kg while fuel still takes 40.9% of MTOW against 46.1% for the remaining empty structure. Under beam theory (Derived from Raymer 2ed, Eqs. 14.35-14.36 (pp. 383-384) for an idealised two-cap beam), the al_2024_t3 spar reaches a peak bending stress of 306.6 MPa against an allowable stress of 337.8 MPa (0.10 safety margin) with a 741.4 mm tip deflection. Verification with Timoshenko beam FEA (NumPy direct stiffness) shows 99.2% stress agreement (304.2 MPa peak von Mises stress, 0.11 safety margin) and 98.9% deflection agreement (749.5 mm tip deflection), though cap crippling is not modelled and assumptions rely on chart-estimated values for L/D max and thickness-to-chord ratio.

## Assumptions
- Cruise at L/D max = 11; loiter at 0.866 L/D max (Raymer 2ed, Ch. 3 (p. 22))
- Loiter speed = 0.75 x cruise speed
- Spar = 8.5% of statistical empty weight on lap 0 (Assumption (Spiral): not from a textbook table)
- Cruise flown at 75% of installed power
- Stall wing loading at ISA sea-level density (1.225 kg/m^3)
- Ultimate manoeuvring load factor n_ult = 5.70
- Cantilever wing root at y = 0 m; aero lift carried 100% by main spar
- No inertia relief from wing structure or fuel (conservative)
- Ultimate load = 1.5 x limit load (Raymer 2ed, p. 335)
- Spar depth = 85% of local aerofoil thickness; cap width = 35% of depth
- Caps sized at ultimate load to compression yield F_cy = 338 MPa (compression cap governs; crippling not modelled)
- Tension cap margin against F_tu = 483 MPa: +0.57
- Web: no shear failure (F_su = 234 MPa) and no shear buckling, unstiffened panel, K = 4.8 (classical long simply supported panel; Raymer gives K as a chart, Fig. 14.42)
- Minimum gauges: cap >= 2.0 mm, web >= 1.5 mm (assumption)
- Mass counts caps and web only: no stiffeners, ribs or fittings
- Tail moment arm = 52% of fuselage length (Raymer 2ed Table 6.4 typical arm ratio)
- Wing configuration: high wing
- Lofted 12-vertex tapered I-beam across 21 spanwise stations (y = 0 to 7.58 m)
- Includes 1.38x structural non-optimum mass factor for root carry-through fittings and web stiffeners
- Clamped root boundary condition (w = 0, dw/dy = 0) at wing root y = 0 m
- Timoshenko shear deformation factor Phi_e = 12*E*I / (G*A_web*L_e^2) per tapered element
- 3D von Mises stress recovery across outer flange fiber, web-flange fillet, and neutral axis

## Warnings
- Web shear buckling sets the web thickness at 17 of 21 stations

## Discussion
### What drove the design
The non-stop 5,570 km range requirement and 45.0 min reserve at a cruise L/D max of 11.0 (Raymer 2ed, Ch. 3 (p. 22)) and a BSFC of 6.8e-08 kg/J drive a cruise mass fraction of 0.6557 and a total fuel mass of 990.8 kg, which far exceeds the 222.0 kg payload (1 crew at 86.0 kg, 1.0 passenger at 86.0 kg, and 50.0 kg baggage). The 28.3 m/s (under 55 kt) stall speed requirement with a maximum lift coefficient of 1.6 limits wing loading to 785.0 Pa (Raymer 2ed, Eq. 5.6 (p. 85)), requiring a 30.27 m2 wing area and a 15.17 m span at an aspect ratio of 7.6. Structural sizing of the cantilever spar is governed by the 5.7 g ultimate load factor (3.8 g limit with a 1.5 ultimate factor) and conservative loading with no inertia relief from wing structure or fuel, while web shear buckling sets the web thickness at 17 of 21 spanwise stations.

### Trade-offs
Feeding the beam-theory spar mass back into the sizing loop reduced the spar allocation from the statistical estimate of 103.6 kg (and 96.0 kg on lap 0) to 92.8 kg on lap 2, trimming MTOW to 2,421.9 kg while fuel still takes 40.9% of MTOW against 46.1% for the remaining empty structure. Under beam theory (Derived from Raymer 2ed, Eqs. 14.35-14.36 (pp. 383-384) for an idealised two-cap beam), the al_2024_t3 spar reaches a peak bending stress of 306.6 MPa against an allowable stress of 337.8 MPa (0.10 safety margin) with a 741.4 mm tip deflection. Verification with Timoshenko beam FEA (NumPy direct stiffness) shows 99.2% stress agreement (304.2 MPa peak von Mises stress, 0.11 safety margin) and 98.9% deflection agreement (749.5 mm tip deflection), though cap crippling is not modelled and assumptions rely on chart-estimated values for L/D max and thickness-to-chord ratio.

## Assumptions
- Cruise at L/D max = 11; loiter at 0.866 L/D max (Raymer 2ed, Ch. 3 (p. 22))
- Loiter speed = 0.75 x cruise speed
- Spar = 8.5% of statistical empty weight on lap 0 (Assumption (Spiral): not from a textbook table)
- Cruise flown at 75% of installed power
- Stall wing loading at ISA sea-level density (1.225 kg/m^3)
- Ultimate manoeuvring load factor n_ult = 5.70
- Cantilever wing root at y = 0 m; aero lift carried 100% by main spar
- No inertia relief from wing structure or fuel (conservative)
- Ultimate load = 1.5 x limit load (Raymer 2ed, p. 335)
- Spar depth = 85% of local aerofoil thickness; cap width = 35% of depth
- Caps sized at ultimate load to compression yield F_cy = 338 MPa (compression cap governs; crippling not modelled)
- Tension cap margin against F_tu = 483 MPa: +0.57
- Web: no shear failure (F_su = 234 MPa) and no shear buckling, unstiffened panel, K = 4.8 (classical long simply supported panel; Raymer gives K as a chart, Fig. 14.42)
- Minimum gauges: cap >= 2.0 mm, web >= 1.5 mm (assumption)
- Mass counts caps and web only: no stiffeners, ribs or fittings
- Tail moment arm = 52% of fuselage length (Raymer 2ed Table 6.4 typical arm ratio)
- Wing configuration: high wing
- Lofted 12-vertex tapered I-beam across 21 spanwise stations (y = 0 to 7.58 m)
- Includes 1.38x structural non-optimum mass factor for root carry-through fittings and web stiffeners
- Clamped root boundary condition (w = 0, dw/dy = 0) at wing root y = 0 m
- Timoshenko shear deformation factor Phi_e = 12*E*I / (G*A_web*L_e^2) per tapered element
- 3D von Mises stress recovery across outer flange fiber, web-flange fillet, and neutral axis

## Warnings
- Web shear buckling sets the web thickness at 17 of 21 stations
